questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
It prevents the trailer from being released by accident
It prevents the vehicle from going too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. It closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full trailers attached.
questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no trailer attached. When driving a bobtail, remember that stopping is harder and takes longer than when a loaded trailer is attached.

questions.question: If air lines are color-coded, what color marks service lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue marks service lines and red marks emergency lines.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than normal
Push the brake pedal as you normally would
Push the brake pedal lighter than normal

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would
questions.explanation: Use the same braking technique with ABS as you would without it. Apply your brakes normally.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in the "emergency" position:

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will apply
The air supply to the trailer will increase

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will apply
questions.explanation: If the air supply control is set to "emergency", the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: If you are not sure if a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes
questions.explanation: If you do not know whether a trailer has ABS, look underneath for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: A trailer hand valve should:

options.text: Only be used to test trailer brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Only be used to test trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (trolley valve) should only be used to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release the brakes.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and connects to the ____ valves.
questions.correctAnswerText: Relay
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer may:

options.text: Be easier to steer during turns

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean during turns
questions.explanation: Putting weight on one side of a trailer causes it to lean to that side. This increases the risk of rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle with stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low traction
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. With less weight, the stiff springs and strong brakes have lower traction than with more weight.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
A valve that shows the fuel level
A valve that limits how much cargo you can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar is a hand valve used to control the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause the vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from driving too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if the air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in its ____ position.
questions.correctAnswerText: Normal
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, turn the steering wheel:

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the direction opposite of where you want the trailer to move.
To the left until backing is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction opposite of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the steering wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require less skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: During a trip, the ____ should be open.
questions.correctAnswerText: Inner shut-off valves
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, keep all shut-off valves open except the ones on the rear of the last trailer. This allows air to reach all the brakes and prevents air from escaping from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: Before a trip, check that air flows to all trailers by:

options.text: Checking for moving air inside each trailer.
Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feeling for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build, then send air to the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If you hear air escaping from these valves, the air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to turn off the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: If you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding, it will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Continue the skid.
questions.explanation: If the trailer is skidding, release the brakes to help the tires regain grip. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will make the skid worse.

questions.question: Place the trailer air supply control in "emergency" position to test:
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or put it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.
